data.title: The Actuary's Pen
data.rumour: A retired insurance man drinks alone at the Anchor and tells everyone their odds.
about: A small uncanny story. Emmett Ardley, a retired actuary, pawns the pen he was given when he retired: it writes down how things will end, and it's never wrong, and he'd like it somewhere else before it gets round to him (§{emmettPen}). While you hold it, it writes gloomy notes on your till roll each morning, including which loans will and won't come back.

A few days later he wants it back, over lunch at the Rusty Anchor (§{actuaryAnchor}). Sell it back (Back in His Pocket); put it on the bar and let it write his ending, which turns out to be "Redeemed", and the pen goes quiet (Redeemed); or keep it (The Odds on the Shelf).

actuaryPen.name: The actuary's pen
actuaryPen.effectText: Each morning, it writes down how one pawned item will leave the shop
tells: A black fountain pen with a gold nib, engraved L.P., MUTUAL OF NEW ENGLAND, 40 YEARS.
The nib is wet. You haven't filled it. Nobody has, for some time.

emmettPen.title: Emmett Ardley pawns the pen that knows how things end

text: Emmett Ardley. Forty years an actuary. Do you know what an actuary does? We tell people how likely things are to end. Mostly, very.
This pen was a retirement present. It writes down how things will end. It's never wrong. I would like it to be somewhere else for a while, before it gets round to me.

then.text: Don't leave it near the ledger. It will start on the ledger.

else.text: No. No, I expect that was always going to happen.

actuaryAnchor.title: Mr. Ardley wants his pen back

steps.narrate: The Rusty Anchor at lunch. Mr. Ardley is on his usual stool with a half of bitter he has been nursing since about 2019. Ruthie Kroll is polishing the same glass in front of him, to keep him company.

then.text: You sold it. Of course you did. Somebody had to.
Cheer up, Emmett. It's someone else's problem now.

steps.text: I'd like it back now, please. While I still don't know.
Or let it tell you, Emmett. You've told everybody else theirs for forty years.

then.why: Emmett Ardley bought his pen back

then.narrate: He puts it in his inside pocket and buttons the jacket over it. He looks safer, and not at all happier.

choose.label: Put it on the bar and let it write

then.narrate: The pen rolls to the edge of a beer mat and writes, in neat copperplate: "L. Ardley. Redeemed."
He laughs. Ruthie says she has never heard him laugh. He signs up for her trivia team on the spot and leaves the pen on the bar for you, like a tip.

then.text: Then I hope it's kinder to you than it was to me. It won't be.

toast.then: The pen has written on the till roll: "{loan.who}. The {loan.what}. Redeemed, {loan.due}." You feel, for no reason, a little sad about it.
toast.else: The pen has written on the till roll: "{loan.who}. The {loan.what}. Never coming back." You sigh, and can't stop.

then.toast: The pen has written "nothing pawned, nothing lost" on the till roll, and underlined it twice.
The pen has written today's date on the till roll and drawn a small box round it, like a headstone.
You notice you've been looking at the rain for twenty minutes. The pen is on the counter, looking pleased.

mornings.note: you skipped the errand: you keep the pen, and the gloom
